```{r setup, include=FALSE}
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 13))
NAVY  <- "#1F3A5F"
RUST  <- "#A64B2A"
GREEN <- "#2E6B4F"

METHOD_COLS <- c(
  snaive = "#7A8B9A", sarima = "#5B7C99", xgb = "#C4A35A",
  lgb = "#3D6B4F", catboost = "#6B4C9A",

)
pretty_method <- function(x) {
  dplyr::recode(as.character(x),
    snaive = "snaive", sarima = "SARIMA", xgb = "XGB", lgb = "LGB",
    catboost = "CatBoost", wavesarima = "WaveSARIMA", wavexgb = "WaveXGB",
    wavelgb = "WaveLGB", wavecatboost = "WaveCatBoost", .default = x)
}

plot_mcb_gg <- function(mcb, title) {
  mcb <- mcb %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      label = paste0(pretty_method(model), " \u2013 ", sprintf("%.2f", mean_rank)),
      label = factor(label, levels = label),
      inside = mean_rank <= min(mean_rank) + critical_distance[1] / 2
    )
  cd_top <- min(mcb$mean_rank) + mcb$critical_distance[1] / 2
  ggplot(mcb, aes(x = label, y = mean_rank)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = 0, ymax = cd_top,
             fill = "grey75", alpha = 0.45) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), colour = "#4C6A8A", linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = inside), size = 2.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = RUST, `FALSE` = NAVY), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean rank", title = title) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 42, hjust = 1, size = 9),
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0, colour = NAVY, size = 13))
}

panel_h <- function() {
  v <- tryCatch(as.integer(input$plot_h), error = function(e) NA_integer_)
  if (!is.finite(v) || v < 80) 140L else v
}

# Reserved HTML height: title bar + n panels + gaps. Must match plotlyOutput.
stack_px <- function(n_panels) {
  n <- max(1L, as.integer(n_panels))
  as.integer(80 + n * panel_h() + (n - 1L) * 22)
}

kpss_cv5 <- function(kpss) {
  if (is.null(kpss)) return(NA_real_)
  cv <- kpss@cval
  if (is.matrix(cv)) {
    cn <- colnames(cv)
    if ("5pct" %in% cn) return(as.numeric(cv[1, "5pct"]))
    if (ncol(cv) >= 2) return(as.numeric(cv[1, 2]))
  }
  nm <- names(cv)
  if ("5pct" %in% nm) return(as.numeric(cv[["5pct"]]))
  if (length(cv) >= 2) return(as.numeric(cv[[2]]))
  NA_real_
}

line_panel <- function(x, y, name, col, ylab) {
  plotly::plot_ly(
    x = x, y = y, type = "scatter", mode = "lines",
    line = list(color = col, width = 0.9),
    name = name, showlegend = FALSE,
    hovertemplate = paste0("%{x}<br>", name, ": %{y:.3f}<extra></extra>")
  ) %>%
    plotly::layout(
      yaxis = list(
        title = list(text = ylab, standoff = 10, font = list(size = 13)),
        automargin = TRUE, zeroline = FALSE, tickfont = list(size = 11)
      ),
      xaxis = list(automargin = TRUE)
    )
}

stack_panels <- function(figs, titles, n_panels, xlab = "Time") {
  n   <- as.integer(n_panels)
  h   <- stack_px(n)
  gap <- min(0.055, 0.22 / n)
  p   <- plotly::subplot(figs, nrows = n, shareX = TRUE, titleY = TRUE,
                         margin = gap)
  usable <- 1 - gap * (n - 1)
  h_each <- usable / n
  anns <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    y_top <- 1 - (i - 1) * (h_each + gap)
    list(
      text = titles[[i]], x = 0.01, y = min(0.995, y_top),
      xref = "paper", yref = "paper",
      xanchor = "left", yanchor = "top",
      showarrow = FALSE, yshift = -2,
      font = list(size = 13, color = NAVY)
    )
  })
  p %>%
    plotly::layout(
      annotations = anns,
      height = h, autosize = TRUE,
      margin = list(l = 72, r = 28, t = 28, b = 52, pad = 2),
      hovermode = "x unified",
      xaxis = list(title = xlab, automargin = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    plotly::config(scrollZoom = TRUE, displaylogo = FALSE,
                   modeBarButtonsToRemove = c("lasso2d", "select2d"))
}

plotly_slot <- function(id, n_panels) {
  h <- stack_px(n_panels)
  shiny::div(
    class = "plot-slot",
    style = sprintf(
      "width:100%%;height:%dpx;margin:8px 0 40px 0;overflow:hidden;", h
    ),
    plotly::plotlyOutput(id, height = paste0(h, "px"), width = "100%")
  )
}
```

# 1. Setup and data

This report follows Borah et al. (IEEE Sensors Letters, 2025) in order: missing-value handling, hourly averaging, min-max to $[0,1]$, Haar MODWT **on the training window**, one CatBoost per component, inverse MODWT (additive reconstruction), then conformal intervals.

**Dataset menu.** **Original (paper)** is `CPCB.csv` / `ID1.csv` — already hourly, so quality flags and causal imputation are **skipped**. **Extra: Shillong** and **Extra: Delhi** are 15-min CPCB CAAQMS extracts; selecting them runs the Phase 1a leak-free pipeline (end-labelled hourly mean, causal fill, no test-period leak) into `store/<group>/clean/` so the paper store is not overwritten. AT and RH are plotted in EDA and left out of the models — the letter is univariate.

Sections 1–9 stay on the letter pipeline (Section 4.2 two-sided MRA is the paper plot; AUDIT F1). Section 4.3 reads the Phase 1b **causal** decomposition store. Section 10 holds the extensions (Fourier vs MODWT, other wavelet filters, EMD).

```{r eda-series, echo=FALSE}
s_re <- reactive({
  grp <- input$dataset_group
  if (is.null(grp) || !nzchar(grp)) grp <- "paper"
  sensor <- input$sensor
  pol <- input$pollutant
  shiny::req(sensor, pol)
  if (identical(grp, "paper")) {
    series[[paste(sensor, pol, sep = "_")]]
  } else {
    packed <- tryCatch({
      run_extra <- function() ensure_dataset_group(grp)
      if (isTRUE(shiny::isRunning())) {
        shiny::withProgress(
          message = paste("Preprocessing", grp),
          detail = "15-min → hourly, quality flags, causal fill (once per group)",
          run_extra()
        )
      } else run_extra()
    }, error = function(e) {
      shiny::showNotification(conditionMessage(e), type = "error", duration = 10)
      NULL
    })
    shiny::req(packed, !is.null(packed$series))
    packed$series[[paste(sensor, pol, sep = "_")]]
  }
})
split_re <- reactive({
  s <- s_re()
  shiny::req(s)
  h <- HORIZONS[[input$horizon]]
  chrono_split_tvt(s$y, s$times, h)
})
```

# 2. Exploratory analysis

## 2.1 Full series, then the split

The whole hourly record is plotted first. The chronological split (no shuffle) comes after that: **train** (Haar, scaler, trees) → **val** (early stopping / grid only) → **test** (scores and actual-vs-predicted). Only the training slice is passed to MODWT in Section 4. Test never enters $x_{\min}/x_{\max}$ or the wavelet filter.

Hour-of-day and day-of-week boxes. A U-shape or commute peaks means a daily period of 24.

```{r eda-boxes, echo=FALSE}
renderPlot({
  sp <- split_re()
  df <- tibble(Datetime = sp$t_train, value = sp$y_train) %>%
    mutate(hour = lubridate::hour(Datetime),
           dow  = lubridate::wday(Datetime, label = TRUE, week_start = 1))
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(5, 4.8, 4, 1.2))
  boxplot(value ~ hour, data = df, outline = FALSE, xlab = "Hour of day",
          ylab = input$pollutant, main = "Hour of day", col = "#EEF1F5")
  boxplot(value ~ dow, data = df, outline = FALSE, xlab = NULL,
          ylab = input$pollutant, main = "Day of week",   col = "#EEF1F5")
}, height = function() max(420L, round(panel_h() * 2.8)))
```

The 24-hour cycle in the boxes fixes $S = 24$ for snaive, SARIMA, and the MASE denominator. Weekly effects are weaker here, so $S = 168$ is not forced.

## 2.2 Missing values (paper)

The letter's chain is **missing-value handling → hourly averages → min-max**. Negative concentrations are treated as sensor faults and set to NA before filling. Genuine spikes are not clipped.

```{r eda-missing}
missing_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(series, function(s) {
  tibble(sensor = s$sensor, pollutant = s$pollutant,
         n = length(s$y), n_missing_in_file = s$n_missing,
         n_clipped_impossible = s$n_impossible)
}))
missing_tbl
```

The GitHub CPCB file arrives with no NAs. Long identical stretches at the start of July 2022 look pre-filled; we leave them as they are so the series stays the one the letter used. Remaining NAs (mainly ID1) are filled in Section 3.

## 2.3 Stationarity

The letter does not run these tests. They are here so we can say, for the series on the screen, whether a plain AR on $Y_t$ is even a fair baseline.

Two tests, opposite nulls:

- **ADF.** $H_0$: unit root (random walk). A small $p$-value rejects that — the series is not a pure random walk.
- **KPSS** (level). $H_0$: constant mean. If the statistic is larger than the 5% critical value, the mean is moving.

Air quality often fails KPSS and still rejects ADF: not a random walk, but the winter mean is not the monsoon mean. That is the case where Haar MODWT is useful — $S_K$ carries the slow level, $D_k$ the rest — and where SARIMA is allowed a seasonal difference.

```{r eda-adf, echo=FALSE}
renderTable({
  y    <- split_re()$y_train
  adf  <- tryCatch(tseries::adf.test(y, alternative = "stationary"), error = function(e) NULL)
  kpss <- tryCatch(urca::ur.kpss(y, type = "mu"), error = function(e) NULL)
  adf_p <- if (is.null(adf)) NA_real_ else as.numeric(adf$p.value)
  kpss_stat <- if (is.null(kpss)) NA_real_ else as.numeric(kpss@teststat)
  kpss_cv  <- kpss_cv5(kpss)
  tibble(
    test        = c("ADF", "KPSS (level)"),
    null        = c("unit root (non-stationary)", "constant mean (stationary)"),
    statistic   = c(if (is.null(adf)) NA else unname(adf$statistic), kpss_stat),
    p_or_5pct_cv = c(adf_p, kpss_cv),
    reject_null_at_5pct = c(
      !is.na(adf_p) && adf_p < 0.05,
      !is.na(kpss_stat) && !is.na(kpss_cv) && kpss_stat > kpss_cv
    )
  )
}, digits = 3)
```

```{r eda-adf-read, echo=FALSE}
renderText({
  y    <- split_re()$y_train
  adf  <- tryCatch(tseries::adf.test(y, alternative = "stationary"), error = function(e) NULL)
  kpss <- tryCatch(urca::ur.kpss(y, type = "mu"), error = function(e) NULL)
  adf_p <- if (is.null(adf)) NA_real_ else as.numeric(adf$p.value)
  kpss_stat <- if (is.null(kpss)) NA_real_ else as.numeric(kpss@teststat)
  kpss_cv  <- kpss_cv5(kpss)
  adf_rej  <- !is.na(adf_p) && adf_p < 0.05
  kpss_rej <- !is.na(kpss_stat) && !is.na(kpss_cv) && kpss_stat > kpss_cv
  series_nm <- paste(input$sensor, input$pollutant)
  if (adf_rej && kpss_rej) {
    paste0(series_nm, ": ADF rejects a unit root (p = ", signif(adf_p, 3),
           "), but KPSS rejects a constant mean (stat = ", signif(kpss_stat, 3),
           " > 5% cv ", signif(kpss_cv, 3),
           "). The series is not a random walk, and it is not level-stationary either — winter and monsoon sit at different levels. A plain AR on raw Y(t) is a weak baseline; SARIMA may difference at lag 24; Haar MODWT puts that slow swing in S_K.")
  } else if (!adf_rej && kpss_rej) {
    paste0(series_nm, ": both tests point away from a stable mean (ADF p = ",
           signif(adf_p, 3), "; KPSS stat = ", signif(kpss_stat, 3),
           "). Treat Y(t) as non-stationary. Difference / seasonal difference for ARIMA, or split scales with MODWT.")
  } else if (adf_rej && !kpss_rej) {
    paste0(series_nm, ": ADF rejects a unit root (p = ", signif(adf_p, 3),
           ") and KPSS does not reject a constant mean (stat = ", signif(kpss_stat, 3),
           " vs 5% cv ", signif(kpss_cv, 3),
           "). A short AR on Y(t) is more defensible here, but the daily cycle in the box plots is still there, so snaive and MASE keep S = 24.")
  } else {
    paste0(series_nm, ": ADF p = ", signif(adf_p, 3),
           ", KPSS stat = ", signif(kpss_stat, 3), " vs 5% cv ", signif(kpss_cv, 3),
           ". Neither test is sharp on this window; lean on the time plot and the ACF at lag 24 instead.")
  }
})
```

```{r eda-pacf-cutoff, echo=FALSE}
renderText({

  paste0("PACF cutoff on train only (95% band, max lag ", input$lagmax, "): p = ", cut, " hours.")
})
```

The ACF peak at lag 24 is the same daily cycle as the box plots. Tree models use lag window $p = 24$ (one day). If the PACF cutoff is much larger, $p = 48$ is also tried on training data only (Section 7).

```{r eda-scatter-server, echo=FALSE}
output$scatter_slot <- renderUI(plotly_slot("scatter_plot", 2L))
output$scatter_plot <- renderPlotly({
  y  <- split_re()$y_train
  k  <- input$lagk
  df <- tibble(y_lag = y[1:(length(y) - k)], y_now = y[(k + 1):length(y)])
  p  <- ggplot(df, aes(y_lag, y_now)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.6, colour = NAVY) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, colour = RUST, linewidth = 0.9) +
    labs(x = paste0("Y(t-", k, ")"), y = "Y(t)",
         title = paste("Lag", k, "scatter")) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0, colour = NAVY, size = 14))
  ggplotly(p) %>%
    plotly::layout(height = stack_px(2L), autosize = TRUE,
                   margin = list(l = 64, r = 24, t = 56, b = 52)) %>%
    plotly::config(scrollZoom = TRUE, displaylogo = FALSE)
})
```

At $k = 1$ the cloud is tight: the next hour is close to this hour. At $k = 24$ a second, looser line appears — same hour yesterday. That is the lag set CatBoost sees for each $D_k$.

# 3. Preprocessing

Paper order: missing values → hourly averages → min-max to $[0,1]$.

$$
x_{\text{hour}} = \frac{x_1+x_2+x_3+x_4}{4}, \qquad
x' = \frac{x - x_{\min}}{x_{\max} - x_{\min}} \in [0,1].
$$

The **Dataset** menu decides whether this chain runs:

- **Original (paper)** — CPCB and ID1 are already hourly. Quality masks and causal imputation are **skipped**; values are stored as-is (`skip_preprocess: true`).
- **Extra: Shillong / Delhi** — 15-min CAAQMS. Selecting the group runs Phase 1a: end-labelled hourly mean, bounds/stuck/spike flags, and a **causal** fill fit only before `selection_end`. Output is `store/<group>/clean/` so `store/clean/` (paper) is not overwritten. Full-series `na_seadec` is not used (AUDIT F10).

Min-max is never stored in those files — it is fit on **train only** after the split below.

| Step | Original (CPCB / ID1) | Extra (Shillong / Delhi) |
|---|---|---|
| Clip / quality flags | Skip | Bounds, stuck, PM ratio, spikes |
| Hourly average | Skip — files are already hourly | Mean of 15-min samples in $(t-1\text{h}, t]$ |
| Imputation | Skip | Causal methods M1–M8, train-only fit |
| Stored file | `data/raw/CPCB.csv`, `data/raw/ID1.csv` and `store/clean/` | `store/shillong/clean/` or `store/delhi/clean/` |
| Split | Train / val / test, time order only | Same cut |
| Min-max | **Train only**, inverted after the forecast | Same |
| Haar MRA (Section 4.2) | **Train only** (letter plot; two-sided) | Same |
| Causal decomp (Section 4.3) | `store/decomp/` | Not stored until `run_decomp.R` on that group |

```{r preprocess-status, echo=FALSE}
renderTable({
  grp <- input$dataset_group
  if (is.null(grp) || !nzchar(grp)) grp <- "paper"
  sensor <- input$sensor
  shiny::req(sensor)
  s <- s_re()
  shiny::req(s)
  skip <- identical(grp, "paper") || !sensor_needs_preprocess(sensor)
  tibble::tibble(
    dataset = grp,
    sensor = sensor,
    status = if (skip)
      "original hourly file — quality flags and causal imputation skipped"
    else
      "extra 15-min source — Phase 1a leak-free preprocess (hourly mean + causal fill)",
    n_hourly = if (!is.null(s$n_hourly)) s$n_hourly else length(s$y),
    n_source_na = s$n_missing,
    n_filled = if (!is.null(s$n_filled)) s$n_filled else NA_integer_,
    start = as.character(min(s$times)),
    end = as.character(max(s$times))
  )
})
```

```{r preprocess-extra-na, echo=FALSE}

  grp <- input$dataset_group
  if (is.null(grp) || identical(grp, "paper")) return(NULL)
  packed <- tryCatch(ensure_dataset_group(grp), error = function(e) NULL)
```

Val is not used to set $x_{\min}, x_{\max}$. If a test hour falls outside the training range it is clipped to $[0,1]$ on the normalised scale. That is what a deployed scaler would do.

# 4. MODWT (paper: Haar)

## 4.1 Filters and reconstruction

The letter's wavelet filter $p_m$ builds the details; the scaling filter $q_m$ builds the smooth. Haar (the paper choice) is

$$
p = \tfrac12(1,-1), \qquad q = \tfrac12(1,1).
$$

MODWT does not downsample, so every component has length $N$ and the lag $D_{k,t-1}$ lines up with $Y_t$. Depth in the letter is $K = \ln N \approx 9$. The additive MRA used for forecasting is

$$
Y_t = \sum_{k=1}^{K} D_{k,t} + S_{K,t}.
$$

$D_1$ is the fastest band (hour-to-hour changes). $D_K$ is the slowest detail. $S_K$ is the long-term level. Each component is forecast by its own model

$$
\hat D_{k,t} = f_k(D_{k,t-1},\ldots,D_{k,t-p}), \qquad
\hat S_{K,t} = f_S(S_{K,t-1},\ldots,S_{K,t-p}),
$$

and the point forecast is reconstructed from those component forecasts (Section 5).

The pyramid wraps the series (periodic boundary). That is the **letter plot** (AUDIT F1: two-sided circular MRA). The split still holds test $Y$ out of this figure; the last $2^K-1$ training rows remain wrap-contaminated. Production features are the causal store in Section 4.3, not these panels. Use the filter menu and depth slider to redraw $D_1,\ldots,D_K$ and $S_K$.

## 4.2 Components $D_k$ and $S_K$

Haar is the paper default. The filter menu redraws every $D_1,\ldots,D_K$ and $S_K$ for D4 or LA8 without leaving this section; those families are scored in Section 10. The stack grows with $K$ — use **Graph size** above if a panel is tight, or box-zoom on one band.

```{r modwt-controls, echo=FALSE}

  selectInput("mra_filter", "Wavelet filter",
              choices = c("Haar (paper)" = "haar",
                          "Daubechies-4 (D4)" = "d4",
                          "Least-Asymmetric-8 (LA8)" = "la8"),
              selected = "haar")
)
```

```{r eda-recon, echo=FALSE}
renderText({
  sp   <- split_re()
  K    <- as.integer(input$mra_K)
  filt <- input$mra_filter
  mra  <- generic_mra(sp$y_train, K, filter = filt)
  err  <- max(abs(mra_reconstruct(mra) - sp$y_train))
  paste0("Max reconstruction error on TRAIN (", toupper(filt), ", K = ", K, "): ",
         signif(err, 3), "  (MRA is additive, so this should be ~0). Test was not in the transform.")
})
```

A spike in $Y_t$ appears at the same clock time in $D_1$. That is why a lag of $D_1$ is a usable feature, and why the letter can train $f_k$ separately on each band. Modelling uses $K = 5$ (scale $2^5 = 32$ h, one daily cycle) rather than $K = \ln N \approx 9$: extra levels add one CatBoost each and mostly fit leftover noise.

## 4.3 Leak-free decomposition store (Phase 1b)

Every stored component at hour $t$ is computed from `value_filled_causal` at hours $\le t$ only (AUDIT F1). Two families:

- **Causal coefficients** (`coef_haar_J10`, `coef_d4_J9`, `coef_la8_J8`) — one pass over the series. Haar is additive: $x_t = V_{J,t} + \sum_{j\le J} W_{j,t}$. D4/LA8 use a backward à trous filter (`waveslim` periodic MODWT fails the D1 bump test and is not stored).
- **Trailing-window MRA / MSTL** — two-sided method on the last 2048 hours ending at $t$; only the last row is kept.

Files: `store/decomp/method=<id>__<scale>/station=<s>/variable=<v>.parquet`. The paper group (CPCB, ID1) is in the store. Extra Shillong/Delhi stations are not decomposed until `Rscript run_decomp.R` is run on that group's clean series.

```{r decomp-store-table, echo=FALSE}
}
```

```{r decomp-store-server, echo=FALSE}
output$decomp_slot <- renderUI(plotly_slot("decomp_plot", 6L))
output$decomp_plot <- renderPlotly({
  grp <- input$dataset_group
  if (!identical(grp, "paper")) {
    return(plotly::plotly_empty(type = "scatter") %>%
             plotly::layout(
               title = "Causal store is built for the paper group (CPCB / ID1). Extra datasets need run_decomp.R after preprocess.",
               height = stack_px(6L)))
  }
  stn <- input$sensor
  pol <- input$pollutant
  mid <- input$decomp_method
  sc  <- input$decomp_scale
  val <- input$decomp_validity
  shiny::req(stn, pol, mid, sc)
  df <- tryCatch(
    get_decomp(stn, pol, mid, sc, validity = val),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(df) || !nrow(df)) {
    return(plotly::plotly_empty(type = "scatter") %>%
             plotly::layout(title = "No stored file for this station / method / scale.",
                            height = stack_px(6L)))
  }
  drop <- c("timestamp", "valid_warmup", "valid_basic", "valid_strict",
            "frac_filled_window", "resid", "n_imf_raw", ".valid")
  drop <- c(drop, grep("^valid_warmup_", names(df), value = TRUE))
  comps <- setdiff(names(df), drop)
  comps <- comps[seq_len(min(5L, length(comps)))]
  keep <- isTRUE(df$.valid)
  tt <- df$timestamp[keep]
  figs <- vector("list", length(comps) + 1L)
  titles <- character(length(comps) + 1L)
  s <- s_re()
  y <- s$y[match(tt, s$times)]
  figs[[1]] <- line_panel(tt, y, "Y(t)", NAVY, pol)
  titles[1] <- sprintf("%s %s  ·  %s__%s  ·  validity=%s  n=%d",
                       stn, pol, mid, sc, val, sum(keep))
  cols <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(c(RUST, GREEN))(length(comps))
  for (i in seq_along(comps)) {
    figs[[i + 1L]] <- line_panel(tt, df[[comps[i]]][keep], comps[i],
                                 cols[i], comps[i])
    titles[i + 1L] <- comps[i]
  }
  stack_panels(figs, titles, n_panels = length(comps) + 1L)
})
```

`valid_basic` is the warm-up mask. `valid_strict` also drops hours with `frac_filled_24h > 0.5` or `in_long_gap` (Phase 1a policy). Diagnostics (D1 causality, D2 additivity, D3 edge fidelity) and the cheap LightGBM screen are written to `store/decomp/DIAGNOSTICS.md` and `store/decomp/SCREEN.md`.

# 5. IMODWT

Forward MODWT uses the letter's filters $p_m$ (details) and $q_m$ (smooth). Inverse MODWT uses the same Haar pair, run backwards, and returns the original series from the components in Section 4:

$$
\hat Y_{N+h} = \mathrm{IMODWT}\big(\hat D_{1,N+h},\ldots,\hat D_{K,N+h},\hat S_{K,N+h}\big).
$$

For Haar those MRA components already live on the original time scale, so the inverse **is** the additive reconstruction

$$
Y_t = \sum_{k=1}^{K} D_{k,t} + S_{K,t},
\qquad
\hat Y_{N+h} = \sum_{k=1}^{K} \hat D_{k,N+h} + \hat S_{K,N+h}.
$$

That is `mra_reconstruct` in `R/04_modwt.R`. $D_1$ is still the fastest band, $D_K$ the slowest detail, $S_K$ the long-term level — the same objects $f_k$ and $f_S$ forecast. A perfect inverse on the training window means $\max_t \lvert Y_t - (\sum_k D_{k,t} + S_{K,t})\rvert \approx 0$.

```{r imodwt-check, echo=FALSE}
renderText({
  sp  <- split_re()
  K   <- as.integer(input$mra_K)
  mra <- haar_mra(sp$y_train, K)
  y_hat <- mra_reconstruct(mra)
  paste0(
    "Haar IMODWT on TRAIN only, K = ", K,
    "  ·  max |Y − IMODWT(D_1,…,D_K, S_K)| = ",
    signif(max(abs(sp$y_train - y_hat)), 3),
    "  ·  max |Y − (sum_k D_k + S_K)| = ",
    signif(max(abs(sp$y_train - y_hat)), 3),
    "  (both ~0). Val and test were not decomposed."
  )
})
```

# 6. WaveCatBoost

For each training series: Haar MRA → one model per component → recursive component forecasts → IMODWT / sum (Section 5).

- **WaveSARIMA**: does MODWT help a linear model?
- **WaveXGB / WaveLGBM**: does MODWT help boosting regardless of Ordered vs default?
- **WaveCatBoost**: the paper method.

Baselines without the transform (seasonal naive, SARIMA, XGB / LightGBM / CatBoost on the raw series) stay in the bake-off so a MASE gap is from MODWT, not from a hidden extra lag. All Wave\* models share the same $K$ and $p$ as those trees. Recursive 1-step out to horizon $h$ is paper Algorithm 1, step 14.

# 7. Hyperparameters

The letter does not publish `iterations`, depth, $\eta$, or lag $p$. A small expanding-window grid is run once on CPCB PM2.5, 1-day split, using only the training prefix. The winning $(p, \text{depth}, \eta, K)$ are then frozen for every pollutant, sensor, and horizon.

```{r hparams}
if (is.null(hparams)) {
  cat("No results/hparams.rds yet. Run run_experiments.R from the project root.\n")
} else {
  cat(hparams$reason, "\n")
  if (!is.null(hparams$grid_lgb)) {
    knitr::kable(head(hparams$grid_lgb, 8), digits = 3,
                 caption = "LightGBM time-based grid (train only), best first")
  }
  if (!is.null(hparams$grid_wave)) {
    knitr::kable(hparams$grid_wave, digits = 3,
                 caption = "WaveLGBM K grid at the winning lag / depth / eta")
  }
}
```

Starting grid: $p \in \{24,48\}$, depth $\in \{4,6\}$, $\eta \in \{0.05,0.1\}$, 150 boosting rounds with early stopping. Modelling caps $K$ at 5.

# 8. Forecasts and conformal intervals

The letter's public notebook ([Wave CatBoost.ipynb](https://github.com/jborah2/WaveCatBoost-Time-Series-Model/blob/main/Wave%20CatBoost.ipynb)) Haar-MODWT the **full** series ($K=\ln N$), fits `CatBoost(lags=24, iterations=1000, auto $\eta$)` on each $W_j,V_K$, then Darts `historical_forecasts` (walk-forward 1-step, observed lags, `retrain=False`), then IMODWT. Section 8.1–8.3 use that protocol on CPCB, ID1, and SHILLONG (`Rscript run_paper_protocol.R`). The archived recursive path is the other dropdown item; it is not Fig. 2.

The conformal score (no Gaussian assumption):

$$
CS_t = \frac{|Y_t - \hat Y_t|}{\hat U_t}, \qquad
PI_t = \hat Y_t \pm CQ_t\,\hat U_t,
$$

with $\hat U_t$ a rolling MAE, $CQ_t$ the $(1-\alpha)$ quantile of $CS$ on a trailing window of length $\kappa$, and $\alpha = 0.05$. $\kappa$ is chosen from $\{24,168,336\}$ so calibration coverage is closest to 95%. Lower and upper edges are $L_t = \hat Y_t - CQ_t \hat U_t$ and $U_t = \hat Y_t + CQ_t \hat U_t$.

```{r s8-controls, echo=FALSE}

  selectInput("s8_method", "Model",
              c("WaveCatBoost" = "wavecatboost", "CatBoost" = "catboost",
                "LightGBM" = "lgb", "XGBoost" = "xgb",
                "SARIMA" = "sarima", "snaive" = "snaive"),

)
```

## 8.1 WaveCatBoost: forecast components, IMODWT, vs test

Same protocol as the letter notebook: Haar MODWT on the **full** series ($K=\ln N$), one CatBoost (1000 trees, auto $\eta$, lags 24) per coefficient $W_j,V_K$, rolling **1-step** forecasts with observed lags, then IMODWT. The four panels are the **7-day** test window for PM2.5, PM10, NO2, and O3 on the sensor in the dropdown. Empty panels mean `Rscript run_paper_protocol.R` has not cached that series yet.

```{r s8-four, echo=FALSE}
uiOutput("s8_four_slot")
```

```{r s8-four-server, echo=FALSE}
.paper_wave_slot <- function(sensor, pol) {
  if (identical(pol, "PM2.5") && !is.null(paper8[[sensor]]$methods$wavecatboost$yhat) &&
      !isTRUE(paper8[[sensor]]$methods$wavecatboost$error)) {
    z <- paper8[[sensor]]
    w <- z$methods$wavecatboost
    return(list(t_test = z$t_test, y_test = z$y_test, yhat = w$yhat,
                scores = w$scores, lower = w$lower, upper = w$upper))
  }
  slot <- paper8$four[[paste(sensor, pol, sep = "|")]]
  if (!is.null(slot) && !isTRUE(slot$error) && !is.null(slot$yhat)) slot else NULL
}

output$s8_four_slot <- renderUI(plotly_slot("s8_four", 4L))
output$s8_four <- renderPlotly({
  sensor <- input$sensor
  pols <- FOUR_POLLUTANTS
  figs <- vector("list", 4L)
  titles <- character(4L)
  for (i in seq_along(pols)) {
    pol <- pols[[i]]
    titles[i] <- pol
    z <- .paper_wave_slot(sensor, pol)
    if (is.null(z)) {
      figs[[i]] <- plotly::plotly_empty(type = "scatter")
      titles[i] <- paste0(pol, "  (run Rscript run_paper_protocol.R)")
      next
    }
    fig <- plotly::plot_ly() %>%
      plotly::add_lines(x = z$t_test, y = z$y_test, name = "actual test",
                        line = list(color = "black", width = 1.05),
                        legendgroup = "act", showlegend = i == 1L,
                        hovertemplate = paste0("%{x}<br>actual: %{y:.3f}<extra></extra>")) %>%
      plotly::add_lines(x = z$t_test, y = z$yhat, name = "WaveCatBoost IMODWT",
                        line = list(color = RUST, width = 1.1),
                        legendgroup = "hat", showlegend = i == 1L,
                        hovertemplate = paste0("%{x}<br>Ŷ: %{y:.3f}<extra></extra>"))
    mase <- if (!is.null(z$scores$MASE)) sprintf("  MASE=%.3f", z$scores$MASE) else ""
    titles[i] <- paste0(pol, mase)
    figs[[i]] <- fig %>%
      plotly::layout(
        yaxis = list(title = list(text = pol, standoff = 8, font = list(size = 12)),

})
```

```{r s8-avp-server, echo=FALSE}
output$s8_avp_slot <- renderUI(plotly_slot("s8_avp", 2L))
output$s8_avp <- renderPlotly({
  sp  <- split_re()
  met <- input$s8_method
  view <- input$s8_view
  yhat <- NULL
  t_hat <- NULL
  lo <- hi <- NULL
  tag <- NULL

  if (identical(view, "wf7") && !is.null(paper8[[input$sensor]]$methods[[met]]) &&
      !isTRUE(paper8[[input$sensor]]$methods[[met]]$error)) {
    z <- paper8[[input$sensor]]
    w <- z$methods[[met]]
    yhat <- w$yhat
    t_hat <- z$t_test
    lo <- w$lower
    hi <- w$upper
    tag <- sprintf("leaky rolling 1-step  |  MASE = %.3f", w$scores$MASE)
  } else {
    key <- paste(input$sensor, input$pollutant, input$horizon, met, sep = "|")
    z <- if (!is.null(fc_cache)) fc_cache[[key]] else NULL
    if (!is.null(z) && !isTRUE(z$error)) {
      yhat <- z$yhat
      t_hat <- z$t_test

    }

                      line = list(color = NAVY, width = 0.7)) %>%
    plotly::add_lines(x = sp$t_val, y = sp$y_val, name = "val actual",
                      line = list(color = "#C4A35A", width = 0.8)) %>%
    plotly::add_lines(x = sp$t_test, y = sp$y_test, name = "test actual",
                      line = list(color = "black", width = 1.0))
  if (!is.null(yhat) && !is.null(t_hat)) {
    if (!is.null(lo) && !is.null(hi) && length(lo) == length(yhat)) {
      p <- p %>%
        plotly::add_ribbons(x = t_hat, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, name = "PI",
                            line = list(color = "transparent"),

    }
    p <- p %>%
      plotly::add_lines(x = t_hat, y = yhat, name = paste0(pretty_method(met), " (test)"),
                        line = list(color = RUST, width = 1.1))
  }
  ttl <- sprintf("%s %s  |  %s  |  %s",
                 input$sensor, input$pollutant, pretty_method(met),
                 if (is.null(tag)) "no cached forecast — run run_experiments.R" else tag)
  p %>%
    plotly::layout(
      title = list(text = ttl, font = list(size = 13, color = NAVY),
                   x = 0, xanchor = "left"),
      yaxis = list(title = input$pollutant, automargin = TRUE),
      xaxis = list(title = "", automargin = TRUE),
```

```{r s8-overlay-server, echo=FALSE}
output$s8_ov <- renderPlotly({
  sensor <- input$sensor

  hn     <- input$horizon
  want <- c("snaive", "lgb", "catboost", "wavecatboost")

                                          series = pretty_method(m))
    }
    ttl <- paste(sensor, pol, "·  paper notebook protocol: leaky rolling 1-step (full-series MODWT, teacher forcing)")
  } else if (!is.null(fc_cache)) {

                                          series = pretty_method(m))

    ttl <- sprintf("%s %s  ·  test %s (train/val held out of Ŷ)", sensor, pol, hn)
  } else {

  }

})
```

The table mixes two protocols. **Split conformal** bands (`run_conformal.R` / `run_new_dataset.R`) are calibrated on a hold-out 1-step window that does not include the plotted test hours; lower bounds are clipped at 0. The leaky rolling 1-step row is the letter-notebook residual quantile on the plotted window — about 95% coverage by construction, not a deployed interval.

(a) CPCB, (b) ID1, (c) SHILLONG. Prefers the notebook protocol (`K=\ln N`, 1000 trees) when `run_paper_protocol.R` has been run.

```{r s8-conf-server, echo=FALSE}
output$s8_conf_slot <- renderUI(plotly_slot("s8_conf", 3L))
output$s8_conf <- renderPlotly({
  sensors <- c("CPCB", "ID1", "SHILLONG")
  figs <- vector("list", 3L)
  titles <- character(3L)
  letters <- c("(a)", "(b)", "(c)")
  for (i in seq_along(sensors)) {
    sname <- sensors[[i]]
    w <- paper8[[sname]]$methods$wavecatboost
    z <- NULL
    t_hat <- y_obs <- NULL
    if (!is.null(w) && !isTRUE(w$error) && !is.null(w$yhat)) {
      z <- w
      t_hat <- paper8[[sname]]$t_test
      y_obs <- paper8[[sname]]$y_test
    } else if (!is.null(conf[[sname]]$yhat)) {
      z <- conf[[sname]]
      t_hat <- z$t_test
      y_obs <- z$y_test
    }
    titles[i] <- sprintf("%s  %s  PM2.5  7-day", letters[i], sname)
    if (is.null(z) || is.null(z$yhat)) {
      figs[[i]] <- plotly::plotly_empty(type = "scatter")
      titles[i] <- paste0(titles[i], "  — run Rscript run_paper_protocol.R")
      next
    }
    fig <- plotly::plot_ly()
    if (!is.null(z$lower) && !is.null(z$upper)) {
      fig <- fig %>%
        plotly::add_ribbons(x = t_hat, ymin = z$lower, ymax = z$upper,
                            name = "95% PI", legendgroup = "pi",
                            showlegend = i == 1L,
                            line = list(color = "transparent"),
                            fillcolor = "rgba(166,75,42,0.22)")
    }
    fig <- fig %>%
      plotly::add_lines(x = t_hat, y = y_obs, name = "actual",
                        legendgroup = "act", showlegend = i == 1L,
                        line = list(color = "black", width = 1.05)) %>%
      plotly::add_lines(x = t_hat, y = z$yhat, name = "WaveCatBoost",
                        legendgroup = "hat", showlegend = i == 1L,
                        line = list(color = RUST, width = 1.15))
    cov <- if (!is.null(z$coverage_test)) sprintf("cov=%.0f%%", 100 * z$coverage_test) else ""
    wid <- if (!is.null(z$width)) sprintf("  width=%.2f", z$width) else ""
    titles[i] <- sprintf("%s  %s  PM2.5  7d  %s%s", letters[i], sname, cov, wid)
    figs[[i]] <- fig %>%
      plotly::layout(
        yaxis = list(title = list(text = "PM2.5", standoff = 8, font = list(size = 12)),
                     automargin = TRUE, zeroline = FALSE)
      )
  }
  stack_panels(figs, titles, n_panels = 3L, xlab = "Test time")
})
```

# 9. Comparison

MASE uses seasonality $S = 24$, matching the letter:

$$
\mathrm{MASE} = \frac{N-S}{h}\,
\frac{\sum_{t=N+1}^{N+h}|\hat Y_t - Y_t|}
     {\sum_{t=S+1}^{N}|Y_t - Y_{t-S}|}.
$$

MAE and RMSE are on original units after inverting min-max.

# 10. Extensions

Three questions that sit outside the letter: why MODWT rather than Fourier; what another decomposition (EMD) looks like; and whether Haar is special among wavelet filters. All three use the same WaveLGB head, the same $K$ and $p$, and the same 1-day split, so a MASE gap is from the transform.

Run `run_extensions.R` if the tables below are empty.

## 10.1 Fourier vs MODWT

Fourier coefficients are global: a spike at hour 1000 contributes to every frequency bin, so there is no $F_{\omega,t}$ to lag. MODWT keeps the time index, so $D_{1,t}$ is the fine-scale event *at time $t$*.

| | Fourier (FFT) | Haar MODWT (letter) |
|---|---|---|
| Time localisation | None — one coefficient per frequency | Yes — $D_{k,t}$ is indexed by $t$ |
| Frequency localisation | Exact bins | Octave bands, level $k$ |
| Stationarity | Mixes winter into summer | Local in time |
| Lag features | Coefficients are not a time series | $D_{k,t-1}$ lines up with $Y_t$ |
| Reconstruction | IFFT | Additive MRA / IMODWT |

```{r fourier-controls, echo=FALSE}
inputPanel(
  sliderInput("fvm_zoom", "Show first N hours", min = 168, max = 720, value = 336, step = 24)
)
```

```{r fourier-vs-modwt-plot, echo=FALSE}
uiOutput("fvm_slot")
```

```{r fourier-vs-modwt-server, echo=FALSE}
output$fvm_slot <- renderUI(plotly_slot("fvm_plot", 4L))
output$fvm_plot <- renderPlotly({
  s  <- s_re()
  y  <- s$y
  n  <- min(as.integer(input$fvm_zoom), length(y))
  ys <- y[seq_len(n)]
  tt <- s$times[seq_len(n)]

  fft_y   <- fft(ys)
  amp     <- Mod(fft_y)
  top_idx <- order(amp, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(min(11L, n))]
  fft_filt          <- complex(length.out = n)
  fft_filt[top_idx] <- fft_y[top_idx]
  fourier_approx    <- Re(fft(fft_filt, inverse = TRUE)) / n
  mra <- haar_mra(ys, 3L)

  figs <- list(
    line_panel(tt, ys, "Y(t)", NAVY, input$pollutant),
    line_panel(tt, fourier_approx, "Fourier", "#8B0000", "FFT"),
    line_panel(tt, mra$D[[1]], "D1", RUST, "D1"),
    line_panel(tt, mra$S, "S3", GREEN, "S3")
  )
  titles <- c(
    "Original Y(t)",
    "Fourier: top frequencies (no time index)",
    "Haar MODWT D1 (time-local)",
    "Haar MODWT S3 (smooth)"
  )
  stack_panels(figs, titles, n_panels = 4L)
})
```

The Fourier curve is a handful of sinusoids laid over the whole window. Haar $D_1$ is quiet until the event, then jumps. That is the lag-feature argument in one picture.

Same WaveLGB head, Fourier octave bands vs Haar:

```{r fourier-scores}

    dplyr::select(sensor, pollutant, filter, MASE, MAE, RMSE)

    cat("Fourier rows are not in the cache yet. Run run_extensions.R.\n")
  } else {
    knitr::kable(sub, digits = 3,
                 caption = "WaveLGB, 1-day: Haar MODWT vs Fourier bands")
  }
}
```

Haar should win on series with sharp spikes (ID1 in particular). Fourier bands ring around every event, so the lag vector at time $t$ still contains a little of yesterday's spike.

## 10.2 Other wavelet filters (Haar, D4, LA8)

Haar is two taps. D4 (4 taps) and LA8 (8 taps) are smoother octave filters. Reconstruction remains $Y_t = \sum_k D_{k,t} + S_{K,t}$ for every family; what changes is the shape of each $D_k$. Switch the filter in **Section 4.2** to see $D_1,\ldots,D_K$ and $S_K$ for Haar, D4, or LA8. The comparison below is MASE only — same WaveLGB head, same $K$ and $p$.

```{r filter-scores}

} else {
  sub <- fs %>%
    dplyr::filter(filter %in% c("haar", "d4", "la8")) %>%
    dplyr::select(sensor, pollutant, horizon, filter, MASE, MAE, RMSE)
  fw <- sub %>%
    dplyr::select(sensor, pollutant, horizon, filter, MASE) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = filter, values_from = MASE)
  knitr::kable(fw, digits = 3,
               caption = "WaveLGB MASE by filter family — lower is better")
}
```

## 10.3 Empirical Mode Decomposition

EMD does not use a fixed filter bank. It peels off Intrinsic Mode Functions from the data:

$$
Y_t = \sum_{k=1}^{K} \mathrm{IMF}_k(t) + r(t).
$$

IMF 1 is mapped to $D_1$, IMF 2 to $D_2$, and so on; the residue plus leftover IMFs sit in $S_K$. The same WaveLGB head then forecasts each piece.

```{r emd-demo, echo=FALSE}
uiOutput("emd_slot")
```

```{r emd-demo-server, echo=FALSE}
output$emd_slot <- renderUI(plotly_slot("emd_plot", 5L))
output$emd_plot <- renderPlotly({
  if (!requireNamespace("EMD", quietly = TRUE)) {
    return(plotly::plotly_empty(type = "scatter") %>%
             plotly::layout(title = "Install the EMD package to see this plot.",
                            height = stack_px(5L)))
  }
  sp    <- split_re()
  n_emd <- min(500L, length(sp$y_train))
  ys    <- sp$y_train[seq_len(n_emd)]
  tt    <- sp$t_train[seq_len(n_emd)]
  emd_out <- tryCatch(EMD::emd(as.numeric(ys), seq_len(n_emd), boundary = "periodic"),
                      error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(emd_out) || is.null(emd_out$imf) || ncol(emd_out$imf) < 1) {
    return(plotly::plotly_empty(type = "scatter") %>%
             plotly::layout(title = "EMD did not converge on this subseries.",
                            height = stack_px(5L)))
  }
  n_imf <- min(ncol(emd_out$imf), 4L)
  cols  <- c(RUST, GREEN, "#8B0000", "#4B0082")
  figs   <- vector("list", n_imf + 1L)
  titles <- character(n_imf + 1L)
  figs[[1]] <- line_panel(tt, ys, "Y(t)", NAVY, input$pollutant)
  titles[1] <- "Original (first 500 h)"
  for (k in seq_len(n_imf)) {
    figs[[k + 1L]] <- line_panel(tt, emd_out$imf[, k], paste0("IMF", k),
                                 cols[k], paste0("IMF", k))
    titles[k + 1L] <- paste0("IMF", k, "  —  adaptive scale")
  }
  stack_panels(figs, titles, n_panels = n_imf + 1L)
})
```

```{r emd-scores}
fs <- ext_scores
if (!is.null(fs) && nrow(fs) && "emd" %in% fs$filter) {
  sub <- fs %>%
    dplyr::filter(filter %in% c("haar", "emd"), horizon == "1d") %>%
    dplyr::select(sensor, pollutant, filter, MASE, MAE, RMSE)
  knitr::kable(sub, digits = 3,
               caption = "WaveLGB, 1-day: Haar MODWT vs EMD")
} else {
  cat("EMD scores appear after run_extensions.R (CPCB PM2.5, 1-day only).\n")
}
```

| | Haar MODWT (letter) | EMD |
|---|---|---|
| Basis | Fixed Haar bank $p_m, q_m$ | Adaptive IMFs |
| Mode mixing | No — bands are fixed | Possible |
| Reconstruction | Exact MRA | Exact by construction |
| Cost | $O(NK)$ | $O(N^2)$ in the worst case |

EMD can park a dust-storm and a traffic spike in the same IMF if they share a local period. Haar will not: $D_1$ is always the 2–4 h band. That predictability, and the speed, is why the letter's choice stays the operational default.

---

GitHub hourly files are not the original 15-minute traces. MASE will not match the letter's Table 1 — boosting hyperparameters were never published, and the deep-learning baselines were left out on purpose. Recursive multi-step forecasts accumulate error at 14- and 31-day horizons.
